qs.q: About salivary glands, which of the following statement is true? - (
o: Both sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves stimulate their secretion
Their secretion is mainly under hormonal control mechanisms
Bradykinin decreases their local blood flow rate significantly
The sympathetic system is the only natural pathway for stimulation
Usually mediated by non-specific mechanisms of action
qs.e: Both sympathetic and parasympathetic stimulation increase salivary secretion.

qs.q: Parasympathetic stimulation of the salivary glands results in:
o: A small amount of protein-rich saliva
A large volume of watery, enzyme-rich saliva
qs.e: Parasympathetic activity produces profuse, watery saliva and induces vasodilation.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: GIT Physiology Exam - April 3, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Regarding salivary glands, which statement is true?
o: Saliva contains significant amounts of active pepsin.
Salivary secretion is controlled by hormones.
Salivary glands are innervated by sympathetic nerves.
qs.e: Saliva is hypotonic (lower solute concentration) compared to plasma because ductal cells reabsorb more NaCl than they secrete water. Saliva is primarily regulated by the autonomic nervous system, not hormones.
